verdict.rationale: Runpod documents a REST API v1 that gives "programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources." A live, key-gated REST API with a keyless OpenAPI spec confirms it, and a GraphQL API, CLI, S3-compatible volume API and MCP server cover Pods, endpoints, templates, volumes and registries. None of this is framed as UI parity, and evidence for non-compute console functions is absent. missing for 10: explicit UI/API parity statement, API coverage of billing/auto-pay and account/team settings, documented API management of Instant Clusters, independent hands-on corroboration of parity

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Runpod REST API v1 provides programmatic access to all Runpod compute resources.
https://rest.runpod.io/v1/openapi.json serves the REST API's OpenAPI spec keylessly
Use the GraphQL API to manage Pods, templates, and Serverless endpoints through queries and mutations.
Manage Pods, endpoints, templates, volumes, and registries through the Runpod REST API.
You can manage Pods, Serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, and models, transfer files between your system and Runpod, diagnose issues, and view account information.
